# Questions {#questions}

1. **@Component vs @Repository and @Service in Spring**  
   1. Used for better classification  
   2. We use @Compnent annotation to mark a class and spring managed component. Then only spring will pick up that as bean and register with application context.  
   3. @Service and @Repository annotation are technically same as @Component with different purpose  
   4. @Repository can catch persistence related exceptions and re-through them as Spring DataAccessException   
   5. @Service is just to indicate service layer classes which holds business logic. There is no special need.   
2. **Bean life cycle**  
   1. Initialize  
   2. Inject dependencies  
   3. Call Customer init method  
   4. Call custom destroy method  
   5. Multiple ways to to implement these callback functions  
      1. @PostConstruct and @PreDestroy annotation in the class  
      2. Custom init and destroy methods in bean definition  
      3. InitializingBean and DisposableBean interfaces to be implemented  
      4. Implement set of \*Aware interfaces   
3. **getForEntity vs getForObject in RestTemplate**  
   1. getForEntity returns the response Entity where as getForObject just returns the response pojo   
4. Returning just object as API response vs ResponseEntity  
5. Delete API status code can be 204 \- No Content or 200 \- OK  
6. All the threads in a application are part of server thread pool. So, we should always release the threads if they are blocked.  
7. Read timeout vs server timeout  
8. Session vs jwt  
   1. Jwt is preferred because it is stateless  
   2. Session is established only for particular server  
   3. Scaling will be difficult  
9.   Bearer means what?   
   1. Means you are the bearer of that token. You own it. It is granted for you after authentication. Next it is used only for autorization.  
10. JWT vs bearer token  
    1. JWTs are just a convinient ways of encoding and verifyin the claims. Used for authorization.   
    2. Bearer tokens are just an random arbitrary string with no intrinsic meaning. Used for authorization.
